title: Sell Mineral Rights in Mulga, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Mulga, AL | Jefferson County
metaDescription: Family land or mineral interest near Mulga, AL, a former Jefferson County coal camp? Get a title-checked offer before you sign anything else.
heroLead: Mulga started as a coal company town west of Birmingham, and the mineral ownership under and around it still carries the fingerprints of who owned the coal, who owned the surface, and how rarely those were ever the same party.
intro: Company-town coal camps like Mulga were usually built on land the mining company already controlled outright, coal and surface both, and sold or released the surface lots to workers and later residents while frequently keeping the mineral estate for itself. If your family bought a home lot in or around Mulga generations ago, there's a real chance the coal and gas underneath was never part of that purchase — and separately, a real chance a different ancestor held minerals on outlying farmland that was never part of the company's original holdings at all.

sections.heading: Company-Town Land vs. Outlying Farm Tracts
paragraphs: These are two different situations with two different answers, and they get confused constantly. A lot inside the old company town boundary likely has severed minerals owned by a mining or land company; a farm tract on the edge of Mulga may never have been split at all. We check the specific parcel, not the general reputation of the area, before telling you which one applies to your family's land.

sections.heading: Confirming What Survived Into the Present Day
paragraphs: Mineral ownership from the coal-camp era has often changed hands several times as the original mining companies sold off, merged, or dissolved, and some of those old interests eventually got leased for coalbed methane by whoever ended up holding them. Tracing that chain at the Jefferson County Courthouse is exactly the work we do before we make an offer on anything tied to Mulga.

faqs.question: Our family bought a house lot in Mulga decades ago. Do we own the minerals under it?
faqs.answer: Possibly not — company-town lots often had the mineral estate reserved by the coal company at the time of sale. We check the specific deed before we tell you either way.

faqs.question: We have farmland on the edge of Mulga, not a town lot. Is that different?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. Outlying farm tracts weren't always part of the company's original holdings, so the mineral estate may never have been severed. We verify this at the courthouse.

faqs.question: The mining company that originally owned this is long gone. Does that complicate things?
faqs.answer: It adds a step, since we have to trace who the interest sold or passed to, but it doesn't make the interest unsellable. We do that tracing ourselves.
